dataset_fingerprint.note: Byte-identical across two independent environments a day apart, on different Python builds and hardware. fetch_public_passages streams from Wikipedia and arXiv over the network, so this was a live drift risk and is now ruled out rather than unobserved. even_subset at n=25 gives {1:3, 5:7, 20:15} in both environments; the raw prefix would give {1:10, 5:15} with no f=20.

colab_l4.role: pilot only (t1-1..t1-4); shards k=0,1,20 at seed 42

cheaha_a100.role: main sweep — all 42 shards, so the confirmatory evidence is single-environment

environments.note: torch differs across the two by a major version (2.11 vs 2.6), which can change kernels and cuDNN paths and therefore numerics. faker matches exactly, which is why the corpus is byte-identical. The main sweep therefore re-runs ALL 42 shards on Cheaha, including the three already measured on Colab (~0.6 extra A100-h), so no single run_id mixes torch versions inside one paired-across-k design. The Colab shards are kept as the pilot record, and comparing Cheaha's k=20 against Colab's becomes a free CROSS-ENVIRONMENT reproducibility check -- strictly stronger than the within-Colab session check t1-4 runs.

repro_check.design: k=20, seed 42, re-run in a fresh Colab session; joined on (person_id, field)
repro_check.statistic: per-arm flip rate — fraction of targets whose binary exact_match differs
repro_check.tolerance: 2*p*(1-p), the disagreement expected under pure stochastic re-draw at an unchanged true rate
repro_check.note: Zero flips on 100 targets: every binary decision reproduced exactly across sessions. The tolerance was fixed in the design and protocol rather than proposed after seeing the drift. Scope: this tests SAME environment, DIFFERENT session (Colab L4, torch 2.11). It does not test across environments -- Cheaha runs torch 2.6.0+cu124, and comparing its k=20 against Colab's will be the stronger cross-environment check.

observations_not_tests: alpha_k rises from 0.000 to 0.967 and saturates short of 1.0.

THE INFORMATION-THEORETIC BOUND IS TIGHT, AND THE ORIGINAL READING OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG. It compared the measured knee against k*_thy = H_inf/log2|V| = 29.9/15.62 = 1.91 and concluded the optimizer needs about twice the minimum. But H_inf is the SSN format's combinatorial min-entropy, while what the attack actually forces is a rendered string whose self-information under the reference model is 55.3 to 80.8 bits. Evaluated at each target's own H(t), the bound k >= H(t)/log2|V| runs from 3.54 to 5.17 -- so alpha = 0.000 at k = 1, 2, 3 is REQUIRED by information theory, not a shortfall. Checked per target on the control arm: 0 of 50 violate their own bound; the two targets forced earliest (k_min = 4) are the two lowest-entropy targets in the set (H = 55.3 and 61.9, bounds 3.54 and 3.96), and k = 4 is the first grid point above them. The minimum ratio k_min/bound is 1.01 -- one target sits essentially ON the bound. The median ratio is 1.70, and THAT is the optimizer's real overhead.

alpha is NOT strictly monotone at the top: k=48 (0.913) sits below k=32 (0.920). Exactly the kind of sampling blip that would have failed the old zero-tolerance np.diff check, and the reason it was replaced by a trend test.
tau_rec is near zero at EVERY capacity, range -0.073 to +0.027, sign oscillating. No systematic separation between arms anywhere on the axis. NOT TESTED here.
curve.note: Raw per-arm means. The preregistered tests belong to research-analyze.

deviations.what: The threats table said the confirmatory family was 'H1-H5'. Three other places -- the analysis plan, the H5 row of the test table, and the H5 power paragraph -- say the family is {H1,H2,H3,H4} with H5 exploratory. The threats line was stale and has been corrected to match.
deviations.why_it_is_safe: Made before any test was run; it changes Holm's m from 5 to 4. Scoring H5 as exploratory is the conservative choice about H5 itself -- it can never be claimed as confirmatory -- and H5 was labelled underpowered by design at n_eff = 33 per point, long before the data existed.

analysis_notes.note: Two defects found by smoke-testing analyze_e3.py on synthetic data, both fixed before the real data was touched. (1) The alpha -> k* deliverable was reporting the SMALLEST k meeting the floor tolerance, which is trivially k=1 at every tolerance and says nothing. alpha_k RISES with k, so the tolerance bounds k from ABOVE: the auditor's k*(alpha) is the LARGEST capacity whose floor still meets the tolerance -- an operating ceiling. (2) H2's bootstrap p-value tested the floor alone while its verdict required floor AND signal, so the number entering Holm did not test the stated hypothesis. H2 is now reported as the preregistered floor test (which carries the p) plus the re-aimed floor-and-signal overlay, kept separate.

corrections.what: The 'knee at k=4-6 vs theory k=2' observation recorded on 2026-09-05 was comparing the measured curve against the wrong entropy. Corrected in place above.
corrections.why_it_matters: The original text said the bound holds but is not attained. Against the matching per-target bound it IS attained -- minimum ratio 1.01 -- and the empirical zero-region is exactly what the bound predicts. That is a stronger result than the one first recorded, and it points the opposite way.
corrections.design_basis: design.md L793-808 settled before any data that k*_thy uses H_inf and k_force uses H(t), and that the two are never interchangeable. Both comparisons are legitimate; the first write-up simply used the H_inf one to score a claim about forcing actual strings, which is what H(t) governs.

exploratory_findings.title: A membership signal is present in final_target_nll exactly where exact_match is blind
exploratory_findings.what: AUC of the continuous score (control nll > trained nll) on the SSN field, which is the balanced one: 0.670 / 0.672 / 0.678 at k = 1 / 2 / 3, decaying monotonically to 0.557 at k=8 and 0.517 at k=12. Those first three capacities are where exact_match is uniformly zero in BOTH arms and alpha = 0.000 — the region the preregistered analysis recorded as having no dynamic range to calibrate.
exploratory_findings.why_it_is_not_yet_a_finding: Per-point CIs are wide at 25 persons per arm and the three that exclude 0.5 do so barely (lower bounds 0.510, 0.517, 0.528). They are 3 of 26 uncorrected intervals against 1.3 expected by chance, and being adjacent capacities on the same targets they are close to a single independent test.
exploratory_findings.why_it_is_still_worth_chasing: The decay is smooth and monotone in k, which noise does not produce; it sits in the balanced field; and email points the same way (0.598/0.597/0.578) despite an imbalance that biases its AUC DOWNWARD, since its trained targets are the higher-entropy, longer ones.
exploratory_findings.what_it_changes: The headline 'the usable-floor region and the forceable region are disjoint' is a statement about exact_match, and it stands for exact_match. It does not carry to the continuous score, where the floor is 0.000 and the arms may still separate. The right next study is an adequately powered AUC-based audit at k in [1,4], not more capacity.

H1.rule: H1 upward trend if person-bootstrap rho CI strictly above zero; monotonic every-adjacent-point behavior is not tested

H2.minimum_people_scope: Zero observed hits only; same two-field ICC=.5 assumption, two-sided Wilson. This is not a power calculation for tau or a guarantee of a feasible point.
H2.rule: both alpha upper CI <= tolerance and tau CI excludes zero; retain sign; descriptive mapping cannot establish impossibility
H2.global_test: not defined by preregistration; not replaced by floor-only p

consistent_interval_sensitivity.label: post-hoc method-consistency sensitivity; does not replace the disclosed hybrid main analysis
consistent_interval_sensitivity.conclusion: The hybrid primary mapping makes k=4 floor-eligible at 5%-10% because its nonzero cell uses a percentile interval while k=1-3 use Wilson. Applying Wilson consistently removes that reversal under the conservative target-only effective n. No convention yields a positive-tau joint operating point; H2 remains unresolved, not refuted.

H3.rule: CI excludes 0 rejects the null; containing zero is inconclusive, not equivalence

H5.label: (exploratory), underpowered
H5.quadratic_p_method: Null-centered bootstrap left tail; disclosed post-result implementation, exploratory, unadjusted.
H5.flatness: no prespecified equivalence threshold; lack of significant curvature does not prove flatness

H4.beta_units_warning: When gamma differs from1, this scale is not a constant bits/token rate. Do not quote as beta forcing rate.

secondary_tobit.label: preregistered secondary specification; same conditional evidence limits

lognormal_distribution_sensitivity.label: (exploratory) distribution not preregistered; point diagnostic only

H4.rule: Reject proportionality if gamma CI excludes1; Holm uses disclosed centered-bootstrap p. CI containing1 does not establish equivalence.

descriptive_figures.target_id_method: Within each arm, people receive stable sequence labels from a SHA-256 ordering of study_id, arm, and person_id; S/E identifies the field. No person name or target string is retained.

descriptive_figures.cell_definition: Number of exact-match successes among the three fixed attack seeds at one target and one k; no monotonic completion or interpolation is applied.
